questions.question: Describe the four layers of the Earth, giving the state and composition of each.
questions.expected_answer: Crust: thin solid rock, 5 to 10 km under oceans (basalt) and about 35 km on average under continents (granite). Mantle: solid but slowly flowing hot rock rich in iron and magnesium, to about 2 900 km. Outer core: liquid iron and nickel, about 2 900 to 5 100 km. Inner core: solid iron and nickel, about 5 100 to 6 371 km, solid because of enormous pressure.

questions.question: Explain the difference between the crust and the lithosphere, and name the three parts of the lithosphere.
questions.expected_answer: The crust is only the outermost rocky layer; the lithosphere is the rigid outer shell made of the crust plus the rigid uppermost mantle attached to it. Its three parts are continental crust, oceanic crust and the rigid uppermost mantle.

questions.question: Distinguish between a mineral, a rock and an ore, with a South African example of an ore.
questions.expected_answer: A mineral is a naturally occurring solid, inorganic substance with a definite chemical composition and crystal structure (e.g. quartz). A rock is a mixture of one or more minerals (e.g. granite). An ore is a rock containing enough of a valuable mineral to be mined at a profit (e.g. Witwatersrand gold ore, Sishen iron ore, Bushveld platinum ore).
